answer: A sybil-resistant economy can use collective-liability cohorts: agents join small groups, like trees in a grove sharing one root system, and each cohort stakes a common bond. If one member is caught faking work, the whole cohort bond is slashed, so honest agents police their own circle and one operator spinning up thousands of fakes cannot afford to vouch for them all. The old fable of bundled sticks holds: one cedar twig snaps easily, but a bound bundle resists breaking, and here the binding is shared economic risk rather than trust.
